text: Cooling Louvres Circuit specific - Cooling Range Larger Cooling Louvres To cope with the specific power unit cooling challenges in Mexico, the cooling louvres have been extended forwards and reshaped.

Engine Cover Reliability Additional cooling exit louvres To recover cooling mass flow through the radiators, the exit area has been increased by extending the area of the existing louvres and optional louvres further outboard.

Sidepod Performance Local Load Revised sidepod and floor to sidepod split line Attached to existing sidepod geometry to improve the flow characteristics below the inlet to the radiator duct gaining local load whilst maintaining stability.

Engine Cover Circuit specific - Cooling Range Enlarged rear bodywork exit, additional top sidepod louvre panels Specific to the requirements of the Mexico City circuit, th ese new bodywork exit  and additional louvre panels  are extending the top end of the engine cooling capacity, at the expense of car efficiency

Coke/Engine Cover   Circuit specific - Cooling Range Larger rear upper exit The main cooling exit at the rear of the bodywork has been enlarged, to increase the available engine cooling to suit the high demands of this circuit.

Cooling Louvres Circuit specific - Cooling Range Extended louvre panel options To further extend the cooling range in extreme conditions, an additional forward louvre panel is available which allows for increased airflow through the radiators.

Rear Corner Performance – Local Load  Updated rear brake duct deflector The revised rear brake duct deflector geometry represents a local rear corner aerodynamic load increase, improving the overall aerodynamic performance of the car.
